$comment: Machine-checkable exit criteria derived from docs/SPEC.md. See SPEC 14.
kind:  'executable' = a test must prove it, and the gate FAILS if no test does.
'manual'     = needs human or visual judgement; tracked and reported, never
auto-passed. Keep this list short and honest - the temptation is
to mark hard things manual to make the board green.
milestone: the milestone by which the criterion must hold. The gate only enforces
criteria at or below `currentMilestone`, so advancing that field is what
tightens the gate. Declaring a milestone done = bumping it and getting green.
Every `spec` value must match a real section heading in SPEC.md - a meta-test checks it.

criteria.statement: SpecReport.Capture declares no package dependency beyond Reqnroll and the BCL.
The Capture assembly file name ends in .ReqnrollPlugin.dll so Reqnroll auto-loads it.
Fixture #1 is real Reqnroll output covering every case the M0 milestone lists.
The sample suite fails exactly the scenarios it intends to fail - no accidental failures.
HTTP exchanges attribute to the correct step under 4-way parallel async execution.
Exchanges made outside any step land in the labelled 'outside steps' bucket, never dropped and never misattributed.
The CaptureScope seeding hook is synchronous - an async hook silently disables ambient capture.
Step keywords are resolved through the gherkinDocument AST join, not guessed from pickle text.
Localized Gherkin keywords survive parsing; styling keys off keywordType, not keyword string equality.
Feature -> Rule -> Scenario grouping is preserved; scenarios under different Rules never merge.
Background steps are identifiable as Background rather than anonymous leading steps.
Hook steps are modelled as first-class timeline rows distinct from Gherkin steps.
Hook rows are labelled from hook type + tagExpression, since hook.name is always empty.
Stream-reported SKIPPED wins over inference; inference applies only where the stream is silent and inferred skips are marked as such.
Retried scenarios group by testCaseId and count once, using the last attempt as the outcome.
Two byte-identical Scenario Outline example rows resolve to distinct scenario identities.
A truncated NDJSON stream parses best-effort without throwing, and reports what it skipped.
Unknown envelope types and unknown JSON properties are ignored rather than fatal.
Data tables and doc strings attached to steps survive parsing intact.
The run timestamp comes from testRunStarted, never from meta (which has none).
Attachment bodies are spooled to disk during parse so peak memory stays O(largest attachment).
The renderer's only input is Cucumber Messages NDJSON.
A run recorded without SpecReport.Capture still produces a complete timeline report.
HTTP evidence is detected by the in-payload $specreport http/1 discriminator.
A JSON attachment with no discriminator degrades to a plain JSON view instead of being mistaken for evidence.
A runmeta/1 attachment surfaces its key/values in the report header.
The emitted HTML issues zero network requests - no CDN, font, image or fetch URL.
Run data is escaped such that a scenario named with a closing script tag cannot execute.
Failed scenarios render expanded and passing ones collapsed by default.
Degraded input produces a visible banner stating what was skipped or incomplete.
Redaction and truncation markers are always rendered, never silently omitted.
Exit code is 0 when a report is produced (even with warnings) and 2 only for no input or zero valid envelopes.
With no screenshot provider registered, capture takes no screenshots and raises no error.
Sensitive request/response headers are redacted at capture time.
Sensitive query-string parameters are redacted at capture time.
Sensitive JSON body keys are redacted at any nesting depth.
Secrets planted in captured traffic never appear anywhere in the emitted NDJSON.
Bodies over the size cap are truncated with an explicit visible marker.
Screenshots are re-encoded to bounded JPEG before attachment.
The README states plainly what redaction does NOT cover.
A directory of NDJSON files merges into one logical run rather than N runs.
Runs are ordered by testRunStarted.timestamp, not filename or argument order.
The matrix distinguishes 'not run' from 'skipped', and 'not run' is excluded from flaky detection.
A scenario that failed then passed within one run is reported as flaky-within-run.
Expand/collapse, filters and the lightbox are fully keyboard operable, and Escape closes the lightbox.
The scale budget holds: 5,000 scenarios / 50,000 steps / 30 runs opens in under 3 seconds.
Oversized output auto-degrades to external assets or omitted attachments rather than aborting.
Status is conveyed by glyph AND text, never by colour alone.
criteria.manualNote: Partly automatable (assert status text present in DOM), but 'reads clearly to a colour-blind user' needs a human look.

criteria.statement: Both light and dark themes meet WCAG AA contrast.
criteria.manualNote: Automatable with an axe/contrast pass later; until that exists, a human checks it and signs off in the release checklist.

criteria.statement: Hook rows are visually de-emphasised relative to Gherkin step rows.
criteria.manualNote: Pure visual judgement. Deliberately NOT faked with a CSS-property assertion, which would prove nothing about how it looks.
